question.problem:
The famous mathematician Alan Turing was born on June 23rd, 1912. Given that January 1st, 1912, was a Monday, use congruences to determine on which day of the week Alan Turing was born.

*Hint: The year 1912 was a leap year since it's divisible by $4$ and is not an end-of-century year.*
question.worked_solution:
We can solve this problem using modular arithmetic.

First, we note the number of complete months between January 1st, 1912, and June 1st, 1912. 

- There were $3$ months with $31$ days (January, March, and May).

- There was $1$ month with $30$ days (April).

- There was $1$ month with $29$ days (February) since it was a leap year.

Therefore, the number of days $d$ between January 1st and June 23rd is given by

$$
d=\overset{\text{days to June 1st}}{\overset{⏞}{31(3)+30(1)+29(1)}}+22.
$$

Now, note that

$$
31≡3,\,30≡2,\,29≡1,\,22≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7).
$$

Therefore, writing the number $d$ modulo $7,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =3(31)+1(30)+1(29)+22 \\  & ≡3(3)+1(2)+1(1)+1\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡9+2+1+1\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡2+2+1+1\, & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the day of the week is the same as the date $6$ days after January 1st, 1912, namely Sunday.
